Classification guard: both authored edges assert association only (etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, hypothesizedOnly:true) - MALIGNANT_TRANSFORMATION for the lymphedema window (HHV-8-driven lymphatic endothelial proliferation occluding the lymphatic lumen) and INFECTIOUS_SPREAD for the cellulitis window. Neither edge is raised to causation: lymphedema may precede the visible lesions and is only partially responsive to tumour treatment, and the cellulitis cohort is hospital-based and confined to HIV-related disease with chronic lower-limb lymphedema in which immunosuppression, interdigital fungal or bacterial portals, and ulceration co-exist unadjusted.

Direction and treatment-state guards: the located literature also documents the reverse temporal relationship - Kaposi sarcoma arising in a chronically lymphedematous limb (PMID 26264753, post-mastectomy lymphedema) - so the lymphedema edge does not assert that lymphedema always follows the sarcoma and the temporal ambiguity is recorded on the edge; because the sarcoma-directed treatment effect on limb volume is small or absent, no treatment-response or aggravation claim is made.

Intermediate-node and duplicate-scope guards: the cellulitis window is authored on this sarcoma primary even though the mechanism routes through lymphatic impairment, because the lymphedema identity is a target-only catalog identity that authors no windows of its own and the infectious risk in sarcoma-affected limbs would otherwise be uncaptured; the lymphedema identity already receives three windows (breast, endometrial, and ovarian cancer) and the cellulitis identity already receives six, so neither target is pre-empted, and no pulmonary, pleural, anaemic, or second-malignancy edge is authored because no condition-specific quantification was located or the identity is absent from the catalogue.
governanceNotes: D1 batch 50 (2026-09-24): two bounded association edges authored - Kaposi's sarcoma to lymphedema (rank 1) and to cellulitis (rank 2) - both ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true; mechanismCategory MALIGNANT_TRANSFORMATION for the lymphatic-obstruction window and INFECTIOUS_SPREAD for the soft-tissue-infection window. The lymphedema proposition rests on the Dauguet 2023 narrative review, which records that lymphedema is a complication of the disease, that HHV-8 has a privileged tropism for lymphatic endothelial cells and induces multicentric endothelial proliferation leading to occlusion of the lymphatic vascular lumen so that obstruction progressively blocks drainage and produces lymph stasis and lymphedema, that the lower limb affected by the sarcoma is usually involved, that lymphedema may appear simultaneously with or after the lesions and may be the first sign long before skin lesions appear, and that it remains a chronic disease whose volume is only slightly reduced or unchanged by treating the sarcoma; on the Brambilla 2006 series of 65 patients with classic sarcoma-associated lymphedema limited to below the knee, in which 60% (30/50) of patients given below-knee elastic stockings had limb volume reduction while all 15 untreated patients had volume increase and no correlation with systemic or local chemotherapy was observed; and on the Lazareth 2002 lymphedema classification, which lists neoplastic disease - naming Kaposi sarcoma alongside breast and prostatic cancer - among the major causes of secondary lymphedema from disruption or obstruction of the lymphatic pathways. The cellulitis proposition rests on the Volkow-Fernandez 2022 series of 39 HIV-positive patients with sarcoma, chronic lower-limb lymphedema, and at least one cellulitis episode (18 patients, 46.1%, hospitalized for the first episode and eight, 20.5%, for recurrence; 14, 35.8%, with recurrence; six deaths, 25.3%, including two from toxic shock syndrome and one from septic shock; associated factors groin or lymph-node infiltration 69.2%, onychomycosis or tinea pedis 44.7%, ulcerated lesions 38.4%) and on the Nazzaro 2018 microbiological study of toe web intertrigo in a large sarcoma cohort, which found significantly different interdigital flora from non-sarcoma patients and states that careful inspection is needed to prevent complications such as cellulitis and sepsis.

Counter-evidence and caveat screens recorded 2026-09-24: (i) temporal ambiguity and reverse direction - lymphedema may be the presenting sign of the sarcoma and the literature also reports sarcoma arising within pre-existing chronic lymphedema after mastectomy, so neither the precedence nor the direction of the lymphedema edge is asserted for an individual; (ii) treatment modification - compression rather than tumour control is the effective management and chemotherapy produces little or no limb volume change, so no causal-reversal or treatment-response claim is made; (iii) multi-factorial infection risk - the cellulitis series is HIV-related and its identified factors include nodal infiltration, interdigital fungal infection, and ulceration, which were not adjusted against one another, and immunosuppression independently predisposes to bacterial infection; (iv) small and single-centre series - the cellulitis cohort is 39 patients from one AIDS cancer clinic, so the incidence in other sarcoma subtypes and in immunocompetent classic or endemic disease is not quantified.

Negative screens recorded 2026-09-24: (i) no sarcoma-to-pulmonary, pleural-effusion, or pulmonary-hypertension edge - no condition-specific quantification of pulmonary involvement as a discrete secondary diagnosis was located in this batch window (zero-record guard); (ii) no sarcoma-to-anemia edge - gastrointestinal involvement with bleeding was not located at condition-specific quantified level and the anemia identity carries windows from its own primaries (zero-record and duplicate-scope guards); (iii) no sarcoma-to-squamous-cell-carcinoma or lymphoma edge - those second-malignancy identities are absent from the catalogue or belong to their own primaries (absent-identity guard); (iv) no sarcoma-to-scars or cellulitis-to-sepsis edge - sepsis is not a catalog identity and scar formation belongs to the wound-healing identities (absent-identity and duplicate-scope guards); (v) duplicate-scope note: the lymphedema identity's three existing windows and the cellulitis identity's six existing windows are not pre-empted; this batch adds the first sarcoma-primary windows to both.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The Dauguet 2023 narrative review of lymphedema and Kaposi sarcoma records that lymphedema is a complication of the disease, that HHV-8 has a privileged tropism for lymphatic endothelial cells and induces multicentric endothelial proliferation leading to occlusion of the lymphatic vascular lumen so that lymphatic obstruction progressively blocks drainage and produces lymph stasis and lymphedema, that lymphedema usually involves the lower limb affected by the sarcoma, that it may appear simultaneously with or after the lesions and may be the first sign long before skin lesions appear, and that it remains a chronic disease whose volume is only slightly reduced or unchanged by treating the sarcoma; the Brambilla 2006 series of 65 patients with classic sarcoma-associated lymphedema limited to below the knee found that 60% (30/50) of those given below-knee elastic stockings had a limb volume reduction while all 15 untreated patients had volume increase, with no correlation to systemic or local chemotherapy; the Lazareth 2002 lymphedema classification lists neoplastic disease - naming Kaposi sarcoma alongside breast and prostatic cancer - among the major causes of secondary lymphedema arising from disruption or obstruction of the lymphatic pathways; the literature documents a frequent, chronic limb-swelling complication with a described occlusion mechanism without establishing that the sarcoma caused an individual's lymphedema.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: lymphedema may precede the visible sarcoma lesions and can be the presenting sign, so temporal precedence cannot establish direction in an individual; tumour-directed treatment may or may not reduce limb volume; regional surgery and radiotherapy independently cause secondary lymphedema in the same populations; filarial lymphatic disease, chronic venous insufficiency, obesity, and primary lymphedema independently produce the same limb swelling; and no cohort quantifies the incidence of lymphedema after a defined sarcoma stage - so the edge records a documented complication at association-only strength.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A tumour-driven lymphatic-occlusion route is described: HHV-8 preferentially infects lymphatic endothelial cells and drives multicentric endothelial proliferation that occludes the lymphatic vascular lumen, and the resulting obstruction progressively blocks lymphatic drainage, producing lymph stasis and protein-rich interstitial accumulation that presents as limb lymphedema - chronic, only partially responsive to treating the underlying sarcoma, and clinically managed with compression rather than cured by tumour control. Because lymphedema may precede the lesions and is modified by treatment, the individual causal contribution remains hypothesized.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Lymphedema is a documented complication of Kaposi sarcoma with a described lymphatic-occlusion mechanism and a quantified treatment series, but individual determination requires histologically confirmed sarcoma with subtype and sites, evidence of lesion or nodal involvement in the draining region, documentation of any surgery or radiotherapy to that region, imaging or lymphoscintigraphy localizing the obstruction, exclusion of competing causes, and review by a qualified medical professional.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Histopathological or immunohistochemical confirmation of Kaposi sarcoma (HHV-8 latency-associated nuclear antigen, with subtype documented where available: classic, endemic, epidemic or HIV-related, or iatrogenic) together with the date of diagnosis and the anatomic sites involved; documentation of cutaneous lesions, nodal or groin involvement, and any visceral disease with imaging or examination findings; the temporal relationship between the sarcoma diagnosis and the onset of limb swelling, including whether swelling preceded the diagnosis; documentation of prior or concurrent surgery, radiotherapy, or chemotherapy to the affected limb and region, and of HIV status and antiretroviral therapy where applicable; limb measurement or lymphedema staging with lymphoscintigraphy or other imaging where available, and laterality of both the lesions and the swelling; exclusion of competing causes of limb swelling (lymphatic filariasis, chronic venous insufficiency, prior surgery or radiotherapy, obesity, primary lymphedema, heart failure, renal or hepatic disease, and deep vein thrombosis); assessment by a qualified clinician of whether the sarcoma and its lymphatic involvement materially contributed to the lymphedema
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Lymphatic filariasis or another infectious lymphatic disease
Chronic venous insufficiency or post-thrombotic syndrome
Prior surgery, lymph-node dissection, or radiotherapy to the affected region
Obesity, immobility, or dependent oedema from heart, renal, or hepatic failure
Primary lymphedema or a genetic lymphedema syndrome
Deep vein thrombosis or pelvic tumour compression unrelated to the sarcoma

evidenceGaps: Histopathological or immunohistochemical confirmation of Kaposi sarcoma (HHV-8 latency-associated nuclear antigen, with subtype documented where available: classic, endemic, epidemic or HIV-related, or iatrogenic) together with the date of diagnosis and the anatomic sites involved; documentation of cutaneous lesions, nodal or groin involvement, and any visceral disease with imaging or examination findings; the temporal relationship between the sarcoma diagnosis and the onset of limb swelling, including whether swelling preceded the diagnosis; documentation of prior or concurrent surgery, radiotherapy, or chemotherapy to the affected limb and region, and of HIV status and antiretroviral therapy where applicable; limb measurement or lymphedema staging with lymphoscintigraphy or other imaging where available, and laterality of both the lesions and the swelling; exclusion of competing causes of limb swelling (lymphatic filariasis, chronic venous insufficiency, prior surgery or radiotherapy, obesity, primary lymphedema, heart failure, renal or hepatic disease, and deep vein thrombosis); assessment by a qualified clinician of whether the sarcoma and its lymphatic involvement materially contributed to the lymphedema
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: a narrative review documents HHV-8 lymphatic-endothelial tropism and lumen occlusion as the mechanism by which Kaposi sarcoma produces lymphedema, a 65-patient classic-sarcoma series documents lower-limb lymphedema treated with compression, and a lymphedema classification names Kaposi sarcoma among the major neoplastic causes of secondary lymphedema. Because lymphedema can be the presenting sign and is only partially responsive to tumour treatment, and because the reverse relationship (sarcoma arising in chronic lymphedema) is also documented, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only, matching the existing breast-cancer, endometrial-cancer, and ovarian-cancer windows on the lymphedema identity.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The Volkow-Fernandez 2022 series of 39 HIV-positive patients with Kaposi sarcoma, chronic lower-limb lymphedema, and at least one cellulitis episode - described as the first study to report chronic lower-limb lymphedema secondary to Kaposi sarcoma as a risk factor for cellulitis - reports that 18 patients (46.1%) were hospitalized for the first episode and eight (20.5%) for recurrence, that six patients (25.3%) died including two from toxic shock syndrome and one from septic shock, that 14 (35.8%) had at least one recurrent episode, and that the associated clinical factors were groin or lymph-node sarcoma infiltration (69.2%), onychomycosis or tinea pedis (44.7%), and ulcerated lesions (38.4%); the Nazzaro 2018 microbiological study of toe web intertrigo in a large Kaposi sarcoma cohort found the sarcoma patients' interdigital flora significantly different from non-sarcoma patients (Trichophyton mentagrophytes 16%, Staphylococcus aureus 14.9%, Pseudomonas aeruginosa 13.9%, Serratia marcescens 5.9% versus S. aureus 26.9%, Candida albicans 22%, Streptococcus agalactiae 7.7%, Escherichia coli 9.9%; P < .01) and states that careful inspection is necessary for early diagnosis of toe web intertrigo in order to prevent serious complications such as cellulitis and sepsis; the literature documents a recurring bacterial soft-tissue infection burden in sarcoma-affected limbs with lymphatic impairment without establishing that the sarcoma caused an individual's cellulitis.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: the located series is single-centre, hospital-based, and confined to HIV-related disease with chronic lower-limb lymphedema, so it cannot separate the sarcoma's contribution from that of the lymphedema, HIV-related immunosuppression, interdigital fungal or bacterial portals, and ulcerated lesions; the reported factors were not adjusted for competing risks; and cellulitis, erysipelas, deep vein thrombosis, and contact or stasis dermatitis independently produce the same red, warm, swollen limb - so no directional claim is made.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized stasis-and-barrier-failure route is described for sarcoma-affected limbs: sarcoma infiltration of lymph nodes and the lymphatic network impairs drainage so the limb becomes chronically lymphoedematous, the protein-rich stagnant interstitium favours bacterial proliferation, and interdigital maceration from fungal or bacterial intertrigo, ulcerated lesions, and skin fragility provide portals of entry; the resulting dermal and subcutaneous bacterial infection presents as cellulitis that recurs and can progress to toxic shock or sepsis, which is why antimicrobial prophylaxis is discussed in the located cohort. Because HIV-related immunosuppression, lymphedema, and fungal portals co-exist and were not separated, the individual route remains a hypothesis.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. A 39-patient series documents cellulitis in sarcoma-related chronic lower-limb lymphedema with hospitalization and recurrence rates, and a microbiological cohort documents interdigital infection in sarcoma patients, but individual determination requires histologically confirmed sarcoma with nodal or groin involvement, independent documentation of lymphedema and of the cellulitis episode with its organism and portal, exclusion of competing causes, and review by a qualified medical professional.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Histopathological confirmation of Kaposi sarcoma with subtype and the date of diagnosis, plus documentation of lymphatic or nodal involvement in the affected limb (clinical examination, imaging, or node histology); independent clinical documentation of chronic lower-limb lymphedema with staging and laterality; the cellulitis episode(s) with date, affected limb, clinical findings, temperature, inflammatory markers, any culture or microbiological result, and the treatment given; documentation of portals of entry and predisposing skin disease (interdigital intertrigo, onychomycosis or tinea pedis, ulcerated or fissured lesions, trauma); immune status including HIV status, CD4 count, and antiretroviral therapy where applicable; exclusion of deep vein thrombosis, stasis dermatitis, contact dermatitis, gout, and erysipelas-pattern presentations by appropriate imaging or assessment; assessment by a qualified clinician of whether the sarcoma and its lymphatic impairment materially contributed to the cellulitis
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Cellulitis in lymphedema from a non-sarcoma cause (surgery, radiotherapy, filariasis, or primary lymphedema)
Cellulitis from another portal of entry (traumatic wound, tinea pedis, onychomycosis, or ulceration) without sarcoma-related lymphatic impairment
Deep vein thrombosis or post-thrombotic syndrome presenting with a swollen painful limb
Stasis dermatitis or contact dermatitis with secondary bacterial infection
Erysipelas or necrotising soft-tissue infection requiring different management
HIV-related immunosuppression with bacterial infection unrelated to the sarcoma

evidenceGaps: Histopathological confirmation of Kaposi sarcoma with subtype and the date of diagnosis, plus documentation of lymphatic or nodal involvement in the affected limb (clinical examination, imaging, or node histology); independent clinical documentation of chronic lower-limb lymphedema with staging and laterality; the cellulitis episode(s) with date, affected limb, clinical findings, temperature, inflammatory markers, any culture or microbiological result, and the treatment given; documentation of portals of entry and predisposing skin disease (interdigital intertrigo, onychomycosis or tinea pedis, ulcerated or fissured lesions, trauma); immune status including HIV status, CD4 count, and antiretroviral therapy where applicable; exclusion of deep vein thrombosis, stasis dermatitis, contact dermatitis, gout, and erysipelas-pattern presentations by appropriate imaging or assessment; assessment by a qualified clinician of whether the sarcoma and its lymphatic impairment materially contributed to the cellulitis
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: a 39-patient series documents cellulitis complicating Kaposi sarcoma-related chronic lower-limb lymphedema with 46.1% first-episode hospitalization, 35.8% recurrence, and 25.3% mortality, and a large-cohort microbiological study documents sarcoma-associated interdigital infection with explicit concern for progression to cellulitis and sepsis. The infection route runs through the lymphedema node, which is a target-only catalog identity that authors no windows of its own, so the sarcoma-primary evidence is authored here rather than left uncaptured; because HIV-related immunosuppression, lymphedema, and fungal portals co-exist unadjusted, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only.
